page.title: Glärnisch — Bächistock (2914 m) via Braunwald — Hike Plan

hero.subtitle_html: Photo via hikr.org - Glärnisch and Bächistock

intro_html:
The Glärnisch massif dominates the Glarus skyline — a broad glaciated fortress rising above the Linth valley that has defined the identity of the canton since the Ice Age. Its highest point, Bächistock (2914 m), is reached by a superb T3 day-hike from Braunwald, a uniquely charming car-free alpine resort perched above Linthal and reachable only by funicular.
— Route compiled from SAC data, hikr.org, and local sources.

The Glärnisch is the largest glacier massif in the Glarus Alps, with three main summits: Bächistock (2914 m), Vrenelisgärtli (2904 m), and Ruchen (2901 m). The massif's glacier is retreating visibly — the ice coverage has shrunk dramatically since the 19th century — making the upper plateau an increasingly rocky landscape that only emphasises the raw scale of the terrain.

The classic hiking route ascends from Braunwald (1256 m) via the jewel-green Oberblegisee (1755 m), one of the finest mountain lakes in Glarus, then tackles the Rüchigrat ridge to reach the broad upper plateau and summit. The hike is serious T3 mountain terrain — sustained, with some steep sections and route-finding — but entirely non-technical and free of fixed ropes. The solitude is striking: this corner of Glarus sees a fraction of the crowds found in the Jungfrau region.

routes.title_html: 2. Variant: loop via Rüti or Klöntal side
bullets_html: Experienced hikers can descend to the Klöntal (Klöntalersee) on the north-west side, or loop via Rüti.
These variants add distance and require careful navigation — consult a detailed topo map.
Not recommended on first ascent or in poor visibility.

getting_there.by_car_html:
Drive to Linthal (Glarus, GL). Parking is available at the Braunwaldbahn valley station in Linthal. Note: Braunwald itself is car-free — you must leave your vehicle in Linthal and take the funicular.

From Zürich: A3 south to Ziegelbrücke, then cantonal road via Glarus to Linthal (~90 min).
getting_there.by_pt_html:
• Train: Zürich HB → Linthal — S-Bahn or IC to Ziegelbrücke, change to the Südostbahn (SOB) / SBB regional train via Glarus to Linthal. Journey ~1 h 20 min–1 h 40 min.
  • Braunwaldbahn funicular: Linthal station → Braunwald (~10 min, runs approx. every 30 min). Buy a combined SBB+funicular ticket or pay separately at the valley station.
  • Plan connections via sbb.ch.
  • Braunwald being car-free is a feature, not a bug — the funicular ride is part of the experience.

day_plans.title: Day Plan — T3 standard ascent (from Zürich)
day_plans.footer_html: Start early if afternoon thunderstorms are forecast (common July–August). The Oberblegisee is best in calm morning light for reflections. Check the Braunwald tourism site for funicular timetables and any path closures.

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: Linthal forecast 18–26 °C → summit Bächistock ≈ 3 °C to 11 °C. Wind chill on the exposed ridge adds a further −3 to −5 °C.

sources_html: MeteoSwiss — most reliable Swiss forecast. Use the Linthal or Glarus point forecast.
Meteoblue Linthal — hourly forecast with mountain specifics.
Thunderstorms in the forecast → postpone. The Glärnisch upper plateau and Rüchigrat are fully exposed with no shelter.
weather.season_html: Summer hike only. Best window: late June to mid-October. Snow typically clears from the Rüchigrat by late June; the upper plateau may hold late-season snow through July in heavy snow years. Check current conditions with SLF and the SAC situation reports.

takeaways_html: Seasonal snow: North-facing slopes retain snow May–early June; crampons may be required.
Local crowds: Less touristic than Säntis; 20–40 hikers/day typical peak season.
Glacio-tectonic geology: Represents key boundary zone; dramatic rock folding (Glarnisch nappe).

reports.title: Bächistock (Glärnisch) — Tagestour von Braunwald via Oberblegisee
bullets_html: Aufstieg ab Braunwald (1256 m) auf gutem Wanderweg Richtung Bleg Alp, dann zum Oberblegisee (1755 m) — traumhafte Spiegelungen am frühen Morgen.
Ab dem See wird das Gelände deutlich alpiner: Rüchigrat, dann halbwegs ausgesetzter Grat hinauf zum Plateau.
Gipfel Bächistock 2914 m — breites Plateau, 360°-Panorama. Abstieg gleicher Weg, insgesamt ~6.5 h.

reports.title: Vrenelisgärtli + Bächistock — Glärnisch-Gipfelsammlung
bullets_html: Beide Hauptgipfel in einer langen Tagestour möglich — Bächistock (2914 m) und Vrenelisgärtli (2904 m).
Zusätzlich ~200 Hm und ~1–1.5 h mehr als die Standard-Bächistock-Runde. Früher Start ab Braunwald empfohlen.
Rückweg via Oberblegisee — Badeplatz für Hartgesottene nach langer Tour.

reports.title: Glärnisch Herbsttour — Stille und Weitsicht
bullets_html: Oktober-Begehung: Gipfelzone bereits schneebedeckt, aber passierbar mit fester Bergsohle. Lärchen leuchtend gelb.
Praktisch menschenleere Route — krasser Gegensatz zum Jungfraugebiet. Perfekte Stille ab Oberblegisee.
Letzter Zug zurück aus Linthal nach Zürich gegen 20:00 — lässt genug Puffer für einen langen Herbsttag.

gear.title: Mandatory
items_html: Sturdy hiking boots (B-grade, ankle support) — the Rüchigrat has loose rock
2–3 L water — no reliable water sources above Oberblegisee
Warm layers: insulating mid-layer + windproof/waterproof shell
Gloves + warm hat — summit can be near freezing even in summer
Phone with offline SwissTopo map + GPX downloaded
Valid SBB ticket + cash for funicular

gear.title: Recommended
items_html: Trekking poles — highly recommended for descent on steep terrain
Power bank (no charging at the summit)

gear.title: Good to know
items_html: Braunwald has a small grocery and several restaurants — stock up / refuel here
No hut on this route; the Oberblegisee is the natural lunch/break spot on ascent

safety_html: Cable aid vulnerability: Wet cables extremely slippery; winter icing impassable.
Summit exposure: Final 100m = T4 scrambling; loose rock common.
Thunderstorm risk: Isolated peak; rapid charge buildup June–August.
Navigation in fog: Fog obscures summit; markers critical.
Rockfall: After rain; upper sections shed water rapidly.
Fatigue on descent: 6–8 hours; lower-limb fatigue increases error risk.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: Compiled from SAC route data, German Wikipedia, hikr.org references, and local sources. Not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions in the Alps change rapidly — glaciers are retreating, terrain is shifting, and path conditions vary by season. Always re-check MeteoSwiss, SLF, and the SAC situation warnings before setting out. Verify the Braunwaldbahn funicular schedule before your hike. If in doubt about T3 terrain, go with an experienced companion or hire a certified mountain guide.
